- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A healthy serving size for a taco meal generally consists of a single taco with a 4-ounce portion of protein (such as chicken, beef, or black beans), a variety of vegetables (such as lettuce, tomatoes, and onions), and a small amount of cheese or avocado.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is recommended to choose whole grain or corn tortillas instead of flour tortillas for added fiber.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Incorporating fresh salsa or guacamole as a condiment can add flavor without adding excessive calories.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Healthier cheese substitutes suggested include:
  1. Greek yogurt as a high-protein, low-fat option.
  2. Nutritional yeast as a vegan cheese substitute that adds a cheesy flavor.
  3. Reduced-fat cheese as a lower-calorie alternative.
  4. Mashed avocado as a healthy source of fat.
  5. Queso fresco as a crumbly Mexican cheese with fewer calories and less fat.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Low-carb tortilla options suggested include:
  1. Lettuce wraps as a low-carb alternative to tortillas.
  2. Low-carb tortillas made with almond flour or coconut flour.
  3. Corn tortillas, which generally contain fewer carbs than flour tortillas.
  4. Cauliflower tortillas using riced cauliflower as a base.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant encouraged the user to experiment with healthier cheese substitutes and different tortilla varieties to make meals more interesting and nutritious.
